title: Host hold -- the one writer a host has, stated on disk by the run that is writing it
description: Written by a run at the moment it becomes a WRITER of the host (never on arrival: a hold written by a run about to be refused is itself a mutation) and CLOSED, never deleted, in a `finally` with its ending. A hold that declares no `released_at` is STANDING, and a standing hold is a door: no machine may decide it is stale, because the bytes of a dead holder and of a slow one are the same. Only a person, by name (`--break-lock <who>`), passes it, and the break is recorded here and in the init journal. Which verbs take it is read from each verb's declarations (ADR-007).

schema_version.description: The ONE declaration of this document's version; the writer reads it from here.

run_id.description: The run that took the hold. Thirty-two hex characters, the width of a receipt's identity.

verb.description: The verb of the run that holds the host -- the run's own verb, never the step inside it that wrote.

owner.description: Who, measured at the boundary; '-' where the host resolves no user.

machine.description: Which machine, as the platform names it. May be empty where the platform names none, and is then shown as such.

pid.description: Which process, on that machine. Reported for a person to check; never probed by the kit.

started_at.description: The moment the hold was taken, from the clock port. Reported so a person can decide; never compared against anything by a machine.

broke.description: Present where this run was started with --break-lock: who declared the previous hold dead, when, and the whole hold that was superseded (null where nothing was standing).

released_at.description: The moment the holder declared its ending. ABSENT is the held state, not a gap.

exit_code.description: What the holding run reported. Written with the release, never before.

ended_because.description: What the run said when it ended badly.
